classification.difficultyReason: Several linked decisions using the demonstrated definitions or procedures. The worked example explicitly brackets mixed operations. The teacher key classifies mixed operations as ambiguous; approved editorial decisions require this book’s convention to be stated in each answer.

content.prompt: Which of these are unambiguous without brackets?

answer.worked: Under this book’s convention: unambiguous. Both $(A\cap B)\cap C$ and $A\cap(B\cap C)$ contain exactly the elements common to all three sets.

Under this book’s convention: ambiguous. Mixed intersection and union need brackets. For $A=B=\varnothing$ and $C=\{1\}$,
$$\begin{align*}(A\cap B)\cup C&=\{1\},\\A\cap(B\cup C)&=\varnothing.\end{align*}$$
The two groupings give different sets.

Under this book’s convention: ambiguous. Mixed union and intersection need brackets. For $A=\{1\}$ and $B=C=\varnothing$,
$$\begin{align*}(A\cup B)\cap C&=\varnothing,\\A\cup(B\cap C)&=\{1\}.\end{align*}$$
The two groupings give different sets.
Under this book’s convention: unambiguous. Both $(A\cup B)\cup C$ and $A\cup(B\cup C)$ contain exactly the elements in at least one of the three sets.
